claims.text: The proposed computational method is based on machine-learning potentials.
Machine-learning potentials can accurately predict the melting temperature of refractory materials.
Machine-learning potentials can accurately predict the entropy of fusion of refractory materials.
Machine-learning potentials can accurately predict the enthalpy of fusion of refractory materials.
Machine-learning potentials can accurately predict the volume change at the melting point of refractory materials.
The machine-learning-potential method has a lower computational cost than the DFT-based ab initio free-energy approach.
The machine-learning algorithms are trained on ab initio data.
Interatomic potentials learned from ab initio data enable prediction of melting properties.
Predicted melting temperatures will be within 10% of experimental values.
Predicted entropies of fusion will be within 5% of experimental values.
Predicted enthalpies of fusion will be within 10% of experimental values.
Predicted volume changes at the melting point will be within 5% of experimental values.
The method will reduce computational cost by at least 50% relative to the DFT-based ab initio free-energy approach.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires errors of at most 10%, 5%, 10%, and 5% for the four properties, whereas falsification occurs only when an error exceeds 15%. Thus, results can violate the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
